claims.text: What US shows here GB and bile ducts: gallstones and biliary obstruct
claims.quote: Gallbladder and biliary tract: For example, to detect gallstones and biliary tract obstruction

claims.text: Kidneys and urinary tract: tells cysts (USU benign) from solid masses (often malig), and finds obstruct such as stones in the kidneys, ureters or bladder
claims.quote: Urinary tract: For example, to distinguish cysts (usually benign) from solid masses (often malignant) in the kidneys or to detect obstruction such as calculi or other structural abnormalities in the kidneys, ureters, or bladder

claims.text: Limit: bone and bowel gas can block the view of deeper structures
claims.quote: With deeper structures, other tissues and densities (eg, bone, gas) can interfere with images.

claims.text: GB Transabdominal US = the best test for gallstones
claims.quote: Transabdominal ultrasound is the best test to detect gallstones.

claims.text: Sonographic Murphy sign: tenderness when the probe presses over the GB
claims.quote: The test may also elicit local abdominal tenderness over the gallbladder (ultrasonographic Murphy sign).

claims.text: Acute inflam: pericholecystic fluid or a thickened GB wall
claims.quote: Pericholecystic fluid or thickening of the gallbladder wall indicates acute inflammation.

claims.text: Kidneys US = the first imaging test for sus urinary obstruct in most pts w.o urethral abnormalities, and looks for hydronephrosis; it avoids contrast and shows kidney atrophy
claims.quote: Abdominal ultrasound is the initial imaging test of choice in most patients without urethral abnormalities because it avoids potential allergic and toxic complications of contrast agents and allows assessment of associated renal parenchymal atrophy. Ultrasound is aimed at detection of hydronephrosis.
